claim: For the canonical Newton–Leipnik flow \(\dot x=-\tfrac25x+y+10yz,\ \dot y=-x-\tfrac25y+5xz,\ \dot z=\alpha z-5xy\), the parameter sign gives an exact compact-recurrence trichotomy. If \(\alpha<0\), the origin is the only bounded complete orbit and supports the only compact invariant probability measure; if \(\alpha=0\), compact invariant probability measures are exactly the compactly supported probabilities on the equilibrium \(z\)-axis. If \(\alpha>0\), every compactly supported invariant probability measure \(\mu\) satisfies \(\mathbb E_\mu[xy\mid z]=\alpha z/5\), \(\mathbb E_\mu[(z+1/20)^2]=1/400+\mathbb E_\mu[x^2]/(5\alpha)\), and \(\mathbb E_\mu[(z-1/10)^2]=1/100+2\mathbb E_\mu[y^2]/(5\alpha)\). Equality in either centered-square lower bound holds only for the origin measure. Consequently every other compact stationary state gives positive mass outside both slabs \(-1/10\le z\le0\) and \(0\le z\le1/5\); a nonconstant periodic orbit that stays in \(z\ge0\) reaches \(z>1/5\), while one that stays in \(z\le0\) reaches \(z<-1/10\).
integrity: All mathematical conclusions are derived from exact Lie-derivative identities and invariance. A dependency-free exact-rational polynomial checker replays the critical identities. No finite numerical experiment is used as proof of an infinite-time statement.
limitations: The theorem concerns compactly supported invariant probability measures and bounded complete trajectories of the canonical Newton–Leipnik flow. It does not establish existence or physicality of a chaotic invariant measure. The 1981 primary article could not be read in full because publisher access required a human verification step; later equation-level reproductions and literature surveys were inspected instead.
title: Exact stationary height defects and a recurrence trichotomy for the Newton–Leipnik flow
